clue.text: Freedom in empty pretentious truisms

indicators.note: in says the freedom word sits inside the two kept letters
empty means the word pretentious loses all its inner letters, leaving its two ends

parts.note: latitude is freedom of action

explanation.surface: A sneer at pompous people who mouth hollow, high-flown platitudes about liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freedom' looks like the subject of the truisms, but it is wordplay; 'empty' keeps just the outer letters of pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: Platitudes are trite remarks, so truisms is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Quiz group of top umpires

indicators.note: group of says a run of letters is gathered from across the words top umpires

explanation.surface: A pub quiz team made up of the best cricket or tennis umpires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group of' signals the hidden letters, spanning toP UMPires.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to question them persistently for information, the verb sense of quiz.

clue.text: Unfinished tomb coated in marble compound

indicators.note: coated in says the shortened tomb word is wrapped inside the stone

parts.note: an agate is a marble, the striped stone used for playing marbles

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for tomb loses its final letter

parts.note: a grave is a tomb

explanation.surface: A half-built tomb faced with a marble composite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' is the verb, as in compound a problem, not a noun for a mixture; agate is a banded stone used for playing marbles.
explanation.definitionFit: To compound a difficulty is to make it worse, which is what aggravate means.

clue.text: Get going and, using every second, firm up belly

indicators.note: using every second says take the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of firm up belly

explanation.surface: A fitness instruction: get moving and tone up that flabby stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every second letter of 'firm up belly' gives I, M, P, E, L.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge forward, making someone or something get going.

clue.text: Short of work experience

parts.note: under means less than or short of, as in under par
go means work or function, as in the engine will not go

explanation.surface: A lament that someone lacks work experience.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to go through or experience it.

clue.text: A noble estate

parts.note: read as the domain, or rank, belonging to one particular kind of nobleman

explanation.walkthrough: 'noble' is the noun, a peer, so the clue asks for the territory or title of an earl rather than a fine country house.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -dom marks a realm or rank, so the earl's domain is his estate and dignity.

clue.text: Long salesperson's talk lacking power

indicators.note: lacking says the letter for power is removed from the sales patter word

parts.note: a sales pitch is a salesperson's persuasive talk
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A rambling sales spiel that has no punch to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is not an adjective for the talk but a verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To itch for something is to long or yearn for it.

clue.text: Letter of thanks following article

indicators.note: following says the thanks word comes after the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A thank-you letter sent after a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Circus school in trendy capital

indicators.note: in says the school word sits within the pair made by trendy and capital

parts.note: hip means fashionable or trendy
Rome is the Italian capital
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A circus school in some fashionable city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a group of sea mammals, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippodrome is an arena for horse shows, and the name is used for circuses and music halls.

clue.text: City allowed to keep Conservative in charge, being diverse

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: to keep says the conservative letter is held inside the word for allowed

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A financial district lets a Tory take charge, which shows its range of views.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcode begins EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclectic means drawing on varied sources, hence wide-ranging or diverse.

clue.text: Fool at university could be swot

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a fool
up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A clown at college could turn out to be a hard-working student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swot' is the British verb for studying hard, not the noun for a studious pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is British slang for cramming or studying intensively, the same as to swot.

clue.text: Sordid stuff: tweet, we hear, going for a song

parts.note: dirt is scandalous or sordid material

indicators.note: we hear says the bird-noise word is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: a cheep is a bird's tweet

explanation.surface: A grubby post on social media that sells for next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEEP and CHEAP sound the same. 'going for a song' is the British idiom for selling very cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going for a song is sold for a tiny price, which is dirt cheap.

clue.text: Made clothes for Dior et al, unusually

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of Dior et al appear in an altered order

explanation.surface: Supplying outfits to a fashion house and its peers, out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' reworks DIORETAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To have tailored something is to have cut and sewn clothes to fit someone.

clue.text: Inspiration seen in opera, 'Tosca'

indicators.note: seen in says the answer is visible inside the words opera Tosca

explanation.surface: Someone finds artistic inspiration watching Puccini's opera Tosca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' signals the letters spanning opERA TOsca.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, the source of poetic inspiration, here for love poetry.

clue.text: Robust, skilful lad losing energy finally perished

parts.note: able means skilful or capable

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the word for lad

parts.note: a boy is a lad

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of energy

parts.note: died means perished

explanation.surface: A strong, capable young man ran out of steam and finally died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes Y from energy, and 'losing' takes it out of BOY to leave BO.
explanation.definitionFit: Able-bodied means physically fit and strong, which is robust.

clue.text: Boasting of a daughter in good show

indicators.note: in says the article and daughter letters go inside the cheer

parts.note: bravo is a cry of good show

explanation.surface: A parent bragging about a daughter's fine performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a show of bold, boastful confidence, so boasting is a close synonym.

clue.text: Environmental concern, a constant international depletion of resources

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
a drain is something that uses up resources

explanation.surface: A worldwide ecological worry about the steady exhaustion of resources.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain, polluted precipitation that harms forests and lakes, is a major ecological worry.

clue.text: Bullfighter turned to drama

indicators.note: turned says the letters of to drama are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A bullfighter changes career to become an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reworks TODRAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull in a Spanish bullfight.

clue.text: Fierce doctor: brief pain is hard

indicators.note: brief says the pain word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: agony is great pain
H stands for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A stern doctor's verdict that short, sharp pain is tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims AGONY to AGON.
explanation.definitionFit: Dragonish means like a dragon, hence ferocious or fierce.

clue.text: Write sad poem the Spanish say is trite, ultimately

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
e.g., for example, is what say means here

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of trite

explanation.surface: A writer of mournful verse declares it hackneyed in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes E from trite.
explanation.definitionFit: To elegise is to write an elegy, a mournful poem lamenting a death or loss.

clue.text: Change man sees in a group

indicators.note: change tells us to reorder the letters of man sees

explanation.surface: A man notices transformation happening in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' reworks MANSEES.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is a French phrase meaning all together, as one body.

clue.text: I'm clear about salvage

indicators.note: about says the letters of I'm clear are turned around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A salvager is sure of their rights over a wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reworks IMCLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim is to recover or rescue something, which is what salvage means.

clue.text: Placid artist turned up, showing original

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
showing says the letters are on display within the words placid artist

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A calm painter arrives and displays a work of originality.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reads LACIDAR, from pLACID ARtist, upwards. The draft gave the hidden step no indicator; 'showing' is it.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical can mean fundamental or innovative, breaking new ground, the sense of original.

clue.text: Arrangement of ornamental edges? Not edges!

indicators.note: Not edges tells us to drop the first and last letters of the word for ornamental edges

parts.note: borders are decorative edges, as on a tablecloth or garden

explanation.surface: A puzzling query about decorative trim, answered with a playful refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not edges' trims BORDERS to its inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Order means an arrangement or sequence, as in alphabetical order.

clue.text: Old-fashioned father drinking endless cha

indicators.note: drinking says the shortened beverage goes inside the father word

parts.note: dad is father

indicators.note: endless says the tea word loses its last letter

parts.note: cha, or char, is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A traditional dad sipping an unending cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha (or char) is old British slang for tea, borrowed from Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated means out of date, belonging to the past, which is old-fashioned.

clue.text: One contemplating heartless go-between

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the thinker word is removed

parts.note: a meditator is one who contemplates

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted thinker acting as an intermediary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle T out of MEDITATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A mediator negotiates between two parties, acting as a go-between.

clue.text: Calculating person's a treacherous type

definitions.meaning: a venomous snake, and snake is slang for a treacherous person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Calculating' suggests scheming, but here it is literal arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: One who adds numbers is an adder, and the viper of that name stands for a snake-like betrayer.

clue.text: Secret look back to find castle

indicators.note: back says the word for a secret look is read in reverse

parts.note: a peek is a furtive or secret look

explanation.surface: Sneaking a glance behind to spot a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PEEK around.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the main fortified tower of a medieval castle, standing for the stronghold.

clue.text: Repeatedly elected to protect Turkey, so critical

indicators.note: to protect says the country code sits guarded between the two copies
repeatedly says the elected word is written twice

parts.note: in means elected, as a party voted in
TR is the international code for Turkey
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: A politician voted in time and again to defend Turkey, so vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' puts TR between the two INs. Turkey is the country, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrinsic means essential or inherent to a thing, close to critical in the sense of crucial.

clue.text: Control movements of river in steep descent

indicators.note: in says the river letter goes inside the plunge word

parts.note: a dive is a steep plunge downward

explanation.surface: Steering a course along a river where it plunges down a falls.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a vehicle or animals is to control and direct where they go.

clue.text: Twice cook old bird

indicators.note: twice says the word for cook is written out two times

parts.note: to do food is to cook it, as in do the vegetables

explanation.surface: Cooking an elderly bird a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old bird' sounds like a tough roast but means an extinct species.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo was a flightless bird of Mauritius, extinct since the 17th century.

clue.text: Authority to sell wood going to royal vessel

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a royal cipher
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: Timber being shipped to a royal yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealership is a licence or franchise granted to sell a manufacturer's products.
